title: The work that slips has no date
mainJudgement: The work that slips has no date.

committeeQuestion.question: Which live control has no implementation date, but still needs a named owner, decision rights and a tested response?
committeeQuestion.why: The CFTC's clearing change has an effective date and an implementation path. Anthropic's announced safeguards and an exploited vulnerability do not give a firm the same clock, even though each requires preparatory decisions now.
committeeQuestion.evidence: The inventory of date-less control changes, named accountable owner, decision rights, readiness milestone, cost or resource assumption, escalation path, test result and closure record.

committeeQuestions.question: For a high-value payment that looks wrong, how quickly can the firm stop it, contact the customer and record the decision?
committeeQuestions.why: The Central Bank of Ireland reports that payment-fraud value rose 27.2% in 2025, with authorised push-payment fraud and cross-border transfers carrying a growing share of loss. Detection is only useful if the intervention route works in time.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The fraud scenario, alert thresholds, hold or release authority, contact path, decision record, recovery outcome and a recent test of the customer-support handoff.

committeeQuestions.question: Can the firm identify whether LiteLLM or Kestra is in its estate, decide what to do and prove the exposure is closed?
committeeQuestions.why: CISA added exploited vulnerabilities in LiteLLM and Kestra to its catalogue. For firms using AI gateways or workflow orchestration, the first control question is not the catalogue entry; it is whether asset coverage and response ownership already exist.
committeeQuestions.evidence: The service and dependency inventory, internet-exposure assessment, named system owner, remediation or compensating-control decision, accepted exception if any, independent retest and dated closure record.

judgement.observation: Anthropic announced Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, with phased rollout from autumn and customer-held activity data. CISA added exploited LiteLLM and Kestra flaws. Ireland's central bank reports payment-fraud losses up 27%, while the CFTC's CAD- and MXN-swap clearing change has a fixed effective date.
judgement.executiveJudgement: The CFTC change is easy to govern: dated, scheduled and owned. The other developments arrive without the same clock. A vendor control is not yet usable; fraud loss measures a customer-authorised decision; exploitation enters the catalogue overnight. The failure is work that matters now but has no deadline, owner or readiness test.
judgement.implication: List three live changes without a mandated date. Name their owner, decision rights, resource and cost assumption, readiness milestone and evidence of a tested response.

topSignals.title: Anthropic announces customer-held AI monitoring, with rollout still phased
topSignals.label: AI evidence and custody
topSignals.why: EFS is announced, not yet generally available. It would place activity data in the customer's cloud account under its keys and route automated flags to its team; the customer also bears cloud storage, read/write and egress charges.
